Redesign Database Explorer UX with user-friendly 'Search Collections'
description:
Replace technical 'embedding set' terminology with user-friendly 'search collections' metaphor. Restructure Database Explorer to make active collection the primary context, simplify tabs, and add contextual help throughout.

## Goals
- Make the concept of multiple AI model indexes understandable to non-technical users
- Elevate active collection to primary context (top of panel)
- Remove redundant model/set selectors scattered across UI
- Add inline status indicators and contextual help
- Reduce cognitive load by consolidating Import + Browse tabs

## Success Metrics
- Users understand they're searching within a specific collection
- Clear visibility of which files are searchable vs not indexed
- Obvious next actions ("Make Searchable" instead of technical jargon)
- Reduced confusion about where to select model/set

## Out of Scope
- Backend data model changes (existing schema is correct)
- Advanced features like multi-collection search comparison
- Dimension customization UI (workaround acceptable)

## Documentation
- **Design Doc**: docs/designs/search-collections-ux-redesign.md
  - Visual mockups of all UI components
  - User flow diagrams
  - Component architecture
  - Terminology mapping guide
  - Implementation phases

- **PR Strategy**: SEARCH_COLLECTIONS_PR_STRATEGY.md
  - Breaks epic into 6 PRs (PR4-PR9)
  - Clear scope and breaking points per PR
  - Dependency chain and merge strategy
  - Size estimates and testing checklists

## PR Breakdown
- **PR4** (brainstrike-f056): Foundation - Embedding set dialogs ✅ COMPLETE
- **PR5** (d537.1-4): Collections selector & terminology (P1)
- **PR6** (d537.5): Files tab context awareness (P2)
- **PR7** (d537.6): Search tab context awareness (P2)
- **PR8** (d537.7-8): Remove redundant controls (P2)
- **PR9** (d537.9-11): Polish, help, and tests (P3)

## Current Status
✅ PR4 complete and ready for review
⏳ PR5-9 planned with detailed sub-tasks

See SEARCH_COLLECTIONS_PR_STRATEGY.md for complete implementation plan.

title: Design and implement embedding set management UI
description:
Create UI for users to explicitly create, name, and manage embedding sets (vector repos). Include: create set modal (name, description, model selection), set list/grid view, active set selector, rename/delete operations. Sets become first-class user-facing entities.

## Implementation Complete (PR4)

### Components Created
Location: `packages/vector-management/src/embedding-set-management/`

1. **CreateEmbeddingSetDialog** - Create new embedding sets
   - Model selection from enabled preferences
   - Name, description, tags, category metadata
   - Auto-populates name from selected model
   - Validates required fields
   - Emits 'brainstrike:embedding-set-updated' event

2. **RenameEmbeddingSetDialog** - Edit set metadata
   - Update name, description, tags, category
   - Model config immutable (shown read-only)
   - Validation for required name field
   - Emits update event

3. **DeleteEmbeddingSetDialog** - Delete sets with confirmation
   - Shows set details before deletion
   - Cascade deletes all chunks in set
   - Confirmation required
   - Emits update event

4. **ManageEmbeddingSetsDialog** - Main orchestrator
   - Lists all sets with stats (chunk count, last updated)
   - Shows model config per set
   - Edit/Delete actions per set
   - "Set as Active" to switch working set
   - Empty state: "Create your first set"
   - Gets available models from preferences (not existing sets)

5. **format-utils.ts** - Shared utilities
   - formatRelativeTimeFromNow() for timestamps

### Integration
- Exported from `@brainstrike/vector-management`
- "Manage" button added to Vector Status EmbeddingSetSection
- Opens ManageEmbeddingSetsDialog
- Uses existing useActiveEmbeddingSet hook for state
- Added EmbeddingSetsRepository export from @brainstrike/db

### Technical Details
- Uses @brainstrike/ui components (Dialog, Select, Input, Button)
- Follows existing vector-status.tsx styling patterns
- Event-driven updates via custom events
- Proper TypeScript types with exactOptionalPropertyTypes support
- Extracted helper functions to meet complexity limits

Fixed to use enabled models from preferences store instead of deriving from existing sets. This ensures:

- Model list reflects user's enabled preferences
- Dimensions come from model registry for local models
- Hosted models use default dimensions (custom dimensions deferred)
